name: Adverb Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Adverb Ventures (adverb.vc), the San Francisco early-stage VC firm co-founded in 2023 by April Underwood (ex-Slack CPO, ex-Twitter) and Jessica Verrilli (ex-Twitter corporate development, ex-GV general partner); the site links to linkedin.com/company/adverb-ventures and x.com/adverbvc, and its team and portfolio pages match the Cooley fund-close release and the SEC Form D filers 'Adverb Ventures Fund I, L.P.', 'Adverb Ventures Parallel Fund I, L.P.' and 'Adverb Ventures Fund II, L.P.' (San Francisco, CA). Press sometimes shortens it to 'Adverb'. Not an advertising agency or ad-tech investor despite the name.

open_items: Fund II size and close not confirmed. The only Fund II record found is a Form D for Adverb Ventures Fund II, L.P. filed 2025-06-18 with a $125,000,000 offering amount, $0 sold and first sale yet to occur (a target, not a close). The lead '$96M closed 2026-06-30' was not found on any fetched page, and EDGAR full-text search (2023-01-01 to 2026-10-30) shows no later Form D or amendment for Fund II.

Fund I close date is the Cooley release date (2023-07-11); the Form D for Fund I and Parallel Fund I was filed 2023-03-23. www.sec.gov refused the declared User-Agent for the Form D documents (the Fund II one was read from a DisclosureQuest mirror; the Fund I mirror returned 403), so Fund I's offering/sold amounts and the main/parallel split were not read.

No application form, pitch address or contact email on adverb.vc: the site offers only a newsletter, community sign-up and careers board, so accepts_cold_inbound and requires_us_entity are 'unknown'. Nothing found on investing in Indian founders.

No sector focus is stated on adverb.vc or in the fund-close release (the firm describes itself by founder insight and craft, not sectors), so stated_sectors is left out. The portfolio skews to AI apps, B2B software, consumer and health, with one industrial name (Foundational Industries). Partner focus_sectors are empty for the same reason; Gary Pesola's bio notes prior work at Conviction, 'focused on AI-native businesses'.
portfolio_count_reported left out: the firm states no count. The portfolio page listed 39 entries on 2026-10-30 (33 named, 6 stealth), with earlier personal angel investments shown separately.

April Underwood's LinkedIn link on her adverb.vc page is malformed ('http://linkedin.com/aprilunderwood', no /in/ path), so linkedin_url is null. Titles come from the Our Team page; the individual bio pages give none.

Arc: Adverb's portfolio lists the company as 'Sparkpoint Inc' (founders Mike MacLennan and Ali Hussain, AI tools for restaurants); the Wilson Sonsini item names the company 'Arc' with the same founders. Arc's website was not found; the full Wilson Sonsini article returned 403, so the round is sourced from its insights listing page.
Centralize: VC News Daily reports '$19M in total funding raised led by NEA' without a stage; it may combine more than one round.

Macroscope seed date not published (Adverb calls it one of its first co-led investments after the firm started). Adverb's participation in Macroscope's $30M Series A (led by Lightspeed) is not stated on any fetched page, so it is not recorded.

Outset Series B: outset.ai/series-b carries no date; month taken from the MrWeb article dated 2025-12-11. The Outset Series A GlobeNewswire release returned 403, so the founder letter (which does not say which investors were new or existing) is the source.
